title.text: Building the technology behind a new kind of business.

text: We develop technology for autonomous business operations, and implement it in businesses of our own.
Operating those businesses gives us a direct way to test what we build, learn from real results, and improve the systems behind them.

about.headline: A software company shaped by the businesses it runs.
about.lead: Digit builds systems designed to handle more of the day-to-day business operations.

text: That includes coordinating work, using specialized agents, preserving knowledge, learning from results, and keeping operations visible.
We use the same technology across businesses in our own portfolio. Our businesses give us a direct environment to test the software, learn from results, and improve the system.
Every operating result becomes input for better software.

headline.text: Build the system. Operate with it. Learn what works.

body: Digit develops the systems behind increasingly autonomous operations and puts them to work inside its own portfolio.
Operating those businesses gives the technology real constraints, real consequences, changing conditions, and results we can actually measure.
The technology evolves around what the businesses actually need, and shapes what we build, improve, and prioritize next.
Over time, the same technology can support other businesses with unique software, infrastructure, and systems built for their operations.

vision.headline: A business should get better at running itself.

intro.text: We're interested in software that automates entire operations, not just tasks.

vision.questions: How does a business move from completing isolated tasks to continuously operating, learning, and improving within defined limits?
body: That is the exact problem we want to solve.
The long-term goal is technology that can take on more operational responsibility while people remain in control of strategy and authority.

items.title: Building for real operations.
items.body: Software built to run businesses should be shaped by real business problems, not only demonstrations.

items.title: Intelligence should compound.
items.body: Results, patterns, and lessons should become part of how the business operates.

items.title: Autonomy needs boundaries.
items.body: Software can take on more responsibility without diminishing its owners' authority.

items.title: Better systems produce better results.
items.body: Our technology creates better decisions, better execution, and better results.
